definitions.name: Hthr
definitions.construction: Source-preserving threshold-extension handle: recover the conditional success probability required in each natural-treatment stratum from a chosen \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\), collect the finitely many response probabilities needed by both experimental tables, and seek one common ordered-threshold private root \(W0\) and one deterministic map \(fY\) realizing all of them without coupling \(U0\) and \(V0\).

definitions.name: Cert
definitions.construction: On input \((A,B)\), compute \((p,r,a,b)\), return compatible exactly when \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\), and, when compatible, return \((qL,qU)\) from their three-branch formulas.

definitions.name: CIout
definitions.construction: \(CIout:=[\max\{0,qLh-6eps\},\min\{1,qUh+6eps\}]\), interpreted as empty if its displayed lower endpoint exceeds its displayed upper endpoint.

statements.statement: For every \(M\in MC(A,B)\), independence gives \(PM(Xn=0,Zn=0)=w00\), \(PM(Xn=0,Zn=1)=w01\), \(PM(Xn=1,Zn=0)=w10\), and \(PM(Xn=1,Zn=1)=w11\). Regime consistency gives \(a=s(0,0)+s(0,1)\), \(b=s(0,0)+s(1,0)\), and \(q=a+b-c+d\). Consequently the admissible success masses are exactly parameterized at the mass-accounting level by \(cL\le c\le cU\) and \(0\le d\le w11\).
statements.justification: This reduction isolates the only two free masses without discarding the independence of the two latent sources.
statements.gap: Generic response-function programs retain many latent probabilities; no checked source states this four-stratum reduction for the two experimental tables.
statements.consumer: The reduction is the symbolic presolver used by the constant-time certificate procedure.

statements.statement: For every strictly positive pair \((A,B)\) with nonempty \(F(A,B)\) and every \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\), determine whether the handle \(Hthr\) can construct one finite \(M\in MC(A,B)\) with mutually independent roots, one private outcome root with at most eight support points, one deterministic outcome function in all regimes, and \(q=a+b-c+d\); if so, provide the construction and verify all eight input cells.
statements.justification: A common finite extension is the nonroutine step separating SCM sharpness from armwise probability completion.
statements.gap: Zhang et al. prove generic finite canonicalization and Duarte et al. prove sharpness of the full program, but neither checked construction gives this bounded source-preserving lift from the reduced fiber.
statements.consumer: An affirmative construction supplies independently checkable endpoint SCMs for an Autobounds regression oracle.

statements.statement: The model class \(MC(A,B)\) is nonempty if and only if \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\), equivalently if and only if \(cL\le cU\).
statements.justification: The theorem turns compatibility of two complete experiments with one SCM into two scalar inequalities.
statements.gap: Gresele et al. formulate causal marginal compatibility and Duarte et al. test feasibility numerically, but no checked source gives this iff frontier for the confounded collider.
statements.consumer: A data-fusion analyst can reject mutually inconsistent experimental tables before attempting causal optimization.

statements.statement: Whenever \(MC(A,B)\neq\varnothing\), the complete identified set is \(QI(A,B)=[qL,qU]\), where \(qL=\max\{a,b,a+b-pr\}\) and \(qU=\min\{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)\}\); every real point of this interval is attained by one finite member of \(MC(A,B)\).
statements.justification: Closed-form sharpness replaces repeated nonconvex optimization by an exact expression with a common-SCM attainment guarantee.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. supply a sharp generic polynomial program and Zaffalon et al. supply approximate multi-source inner ranges; neither checked result states these endpoints or their full source-preserving attainment.
statements.consumer: Autobounds can dispatch this fixed graph and query to an analytic specialization and use the formula as a solver regression oracle.

statements.statement: If every cell of \(A\) and \(B\) is rational and \(MC(A,B)\neq\varnothing\), there exist endpoint-attaining SCMs for \(qL\) and \(qU\) with binary roots \(U0,V0\), a private root \(W0\) having at most eight atoms, rational root weights, and deterministic structural functions; each certificate is checkable by at most \(32\) exogenous assignments.
statements.justification: Exact rational witnesses make sharpness independently auditable rather than dependent on floating-point global optimization.
statements.gap: Generic canonical SCM bounds are finite but much larger and do not furnish this menu-specific rational certificate size.
statements.consumer: A software test suite can validate compatibility, all observed cells, and both endpoint values by finite exact arithmetic.

statements.statement: For the fixed binary graph, \(Cert(A,B)\) decides compatibility and returns the sharp endpoints using a constant number of arithmetic operations and comparisons; for rational inputs it additionally emits the certificates of \(\text{prop:rational-endpoint-certificates}\).
statements.justification: The proposition states the operational gain over invoking a generic polynomial optimizer on every input.
statements.gap: Existing general algorithms emphasize coverage across graphs; the checked literature does not expose a constant-size certificate for this fixed menu.
statements.consumer: Autobounds can use \(Cert\) as a special-case dispatch and as a correctness oracle for its generic optimizer.

statements.statement: For every compatible strictly positive input, \(qU-qL=cU-cL+w11\ge w11>0\); thus the two experiments never point-identify \(q\) in the stated positive-table model.
statements.justification: The width identity distinguishes compatibility from identification and gives a required sanity reduction.
statements.gap: The generic methods return numerical intervals but do not state the strictly positive nonidentification margin for this family.
statements.consumer: An experimental designer learns that these two regimes alone cannot point-identify the joint-intervention risk.

statements.statement: For \(A=((1/8,3/8),(3/8,1/8))\) and \(B=((3/8,1/8),(3/8,1/8))\), both tables are strictly positive, \(cL=cU=1/8\), and \(QI(A,B)=[3/8,5/8]\); the two endpoints admit finite certificates satisfying all eight cells and mutual root independence.
statements.justification: This pinned-fiber instance is the earliest destructive check on the universal extension at a compatibility boundary.
statements.gap: A numerical endpoint alone would not verify that the same deterministic outcome law reproduces both complete tables.
statements.consumer: The example is a fixed exact regression test for implementations of the certificate generator.

statements.statement: Under \(\text{ass:multinomial-a}\) and \(\text{ass:multinomial-b}\), with probability at least \(1-alpha\), \(CIout\) contains the complete population set \(QI(A,B)\), including at endpoint ties and compatibility boundaries.
statements.justification: A simultaneous cellwise concentration layer gives a transparent conservative sampling guarantee without smooth-branch selection.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. project general confidence regions through optimization; this fixed formula admits a direct finite-sample outer interval, but no nominal or optimal inference claim is made.
statements.consumer: Analysts using empirical experiment tables obtain an immediate conservative uncertainty report alongside the population certificate.

sampling_model.design: Two randomized regime studies report complete \(2\times2\) tables, one under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\) and one under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\).
sampling_model.units: The population version treats \(A\) and \(B\) as exact laws of one SCM; the optional sampling result uses multinomial frequency tables of sizes \(nA\) and \(nB\).
sampling_model.treatment: The first regime fixes \(Z=0\) and leaves \(X\) natural; the second fixes \(X=0\) and leaves \(Z\) natural.
sampling_model.overlap: Strict positivity of all eight population cells implies \(0<p,r<1\), \(0<a<p\), and \(0<b<r\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No nuisance functions are estimated. The optional interval uses only empirical multinomial cells and simultaneous concentration.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Minimization or maximization of the produced polynomial program gives sharp lower or upper bounds on the declared target.
Counterfactual consistency of overlapping categorical marginal SCMs restricts the admissible marginal and joint SCMs.
Every categorical SCM has a finite canonical SCM with the same graph and all the same counterfactual distributions.
EMCC returns fully specified compatible SCMs whose counterfactual range approximates the actual bounds from inside.
The global extrema of a response-function linear program occur at vertices of its feasible polytope.

tldr: Two complete experiments on overlapping margins of a binary collider need not arise from one SCM. Under two mutually independent shared roots and private outcome noise, the proposal seeks an iff compatibility inequality and a closed-form sharp interval for the all-zero joint-intervention risk. The decisive open step is a common finite threshold extension that preserves both source independence and one deterministic outcome law. Its resolution yields constant-time endpoints, exact rational endpoint certificates, a positive boundary regression case, and a conservative optional sampling interval, all for this fixed graph only.

project_justification.gap: General discrete-SCM methods can optimize this query numerically, and causal-marginal methods explain why overlapping reports must be consistent, but neither checked line supplies the graph-specific compatibility frontier, analytic endpoints, or a small common-SCM witness.
project_justification.niche: The fixed binary collider collapses to four natural-treatment strata, yet source independence prevents the armwise completions and unrestricted latent couplings used in simpler partial-identification arguments.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the two-mass fiber, resolves its source-preserving finite extension, and packages the resulting iff test and max/min interval as an exact certificate procedure for the same input handled generically by Autobounds.

related_work: Gresele et al. formulate the structural causal marginal problem and show how one shared response-function law constrains overlapping causal models; their main analytic Boolean construction is causally sufficient, while their confounded extension retains a high-dimensional partially factorized law. Duarte et al. prove that discrete causal bounds under observational and experimental evidence reduce to sharp polynomial programs and implement this result in Autobounds; that general theorem informs the present specialization but is not claimed to be tightened. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim prove finite canonical SCM sufficiency for arbitrary categorical counterfactual distributions; the proposed at-most-eight-point private extension is a menu-specific certificate, not a new generic canonicalization theorem. Sachs, Jonzon, Sjoelander, and Gabriel derive tight symbolic bounds for response-function models whose constraints are linear; their elimination logic motivates the four-stratum analysis, while the independent latent-source structure here must be preserved explicitly. Zaffalon et al. fuse heterogeneous observational and randomized studies through causal EM and report approximate inner ranges; their work is adjacent rather than a theorem-level target. Shridharan and Iyengar reduce the degree of multilinear causal-bound programs in quasi-Markovian graphs, but do not state a closed-form solution for this experimental menu. Finkelstein and Shpitser derive inequalities from logical relations among counterfactual events, and Balke and Pearl provide the foundational response-type sharp-bound template for binary instrumental variables; neither checked example matches this collider target.
technical_internal_limitation: The reduction to \((c,d)\) and denominator-eight enumerations are diagnostic evidence only. The universal source-preserving extension must still verify one common deterministic \(fY\), one private root \(W0\), both complete experimental tables, and mutual independence of \(U0,V0,W0\). A correlated-root model can escape the claimed independent-source interval, so replacing the product law by an unrestricted response simplex is invalid.
honest_scope: The compatibility algebra and endpoint projection are the tractable portion; the finite common extension is explicitly open and load-bearing. Structural zeros, correlated or budget-dependent shared roots, different study populations, all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, minimal support, nominal tie-robust inference, general compilation, and any field-tier claim are excluded. If regime \(B\) is omitted, the same mass accounting collapses to the standard missing-stratum bound \(q\in[a,a+1-p]\); symmetrically, omitting regime \(A\) gives \(q\in[b,b+1-r]\). As a second sanity case, the positive boundary tables in \(\text{prop:boundary-kill-test}\) pin \(c\) while leaving the nondegenerate interval \([3/8,5/8]\), so compatibility does not silently become point identification.

seed_details.title: Closed-form compatibility and an attained risk interval for two collider experiments
seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 3--4, Theorem 1, and Section 9 of the arXiv version were checked; the theorem turns discrete causal bounds into sharp polynomial programs and the conclusion identifies analytic simplification as an open direction.
seed_details.opportunity: Eliminate the same-input polynomial program for the fixed binary collider into one compatibility inequality and two three-branch endpoint formulas, with one source-preserving SCM for every feasible target value.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace canonical response-function enumeration by a four-stratum mass reduction that retains the product law of the two latent roots.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for the exact joint-intervention target, the expression \(a+b-pr\), and binary-collider bounds with independent latent roots returned generic bounding papers and collider-bias papers, but no formula collision.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Duarte et al. because their sharp polynomial program already handles arbitrary discrete experiments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their theorem certifies a generic optimization problem; it does not state this compatibility frontier, its closed-form projection, or a common small SCM certificate for every point.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed uses the SCM-native M20 shape, names the analytic fiber and certificate procedure, and does not present generic finite canonicalization as new.

seed_details.title: The simultaneous region of all four joint-intervention risks
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 3.2 constructs one shared Boolean response-function law and projects it to overlapping marginal SCMs; Section 5 notes the doubly exponential growth beyond two causes.
seed_details.opportunity: Describe the joint image of all four probabilities \(P(Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x,Z=z))\), rather than optimizing four coordinates separately.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace scalar elimination in the two-coordinate fiber by simultaneous projection into four target coordinates while retaining one deterministic outcome map.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found Gresele et al.'s projection framework, Duarte et al.'s scalar optimization, and Sachs et al.'s symbolic linear programs, but no joint-image description for this independent-source menu.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate by running a generic optimizer in many directions and intersecting the resulting half-spaces.
seed_details.rebuttal: Finite directional runs do not certify the full image, its facets, or attainment by one source-preserving law; nonlinear cross-coordinate restrictions may remain.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The object is the complete graphical response region, not four repackaged marginal intervals.

seed_details.title: Compatibility and all-zero risk bounds for a three-parent collider
seed_details.anchor_location: The abstract, reduced multilinear-program construction, and conclusion were checked; the objective degree falls with the number of intervened districts, but the method does not give this source-overlap formula.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive an explicit compatibility system and an attained all-zero joint-intervention interval from three single-parent experimental tables.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace two-way interval intersection by elimination on an eight-cell product-source response object.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found generic canonical SCM programs, hyperarc pruning, and approximate multi-study fusion, but no exact three-parent source-specific collider characterization.
seed_details.red_team: A routine induction on the number of parents extends the two-source rectangle.
seed_details.rebuttal: The third source introduces higher-order product constraints that pairwise compatibility cannot detect, so the first elimination step is not inductive.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed names the new higher-order compatibility object and does not promise a general thicket compiler.

seed_details.title: Support-stratified collider bounds with structural zeros
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1 and Appendix A were checked; canonical partitions preserve all categorical counterfactual distributions, but do not classify boundary support faces analytically.
seed_details.opportunity: Catalogue compatibility and attained target intervals on every support mask of the two regime tables.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace division by positive stratum masses with support-mask-specific active-face elimination.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found canonical finite reductions and small latent-variable feasibility methods, but no support catalogue for this two-regime collider.
seed_details.red_team: The positive formulas extend by continuity after assigning arbitrary responses on zero-mass strata.
seed_details.rebuttal: Continuity gives outer limits but does not decide which equalities delete response types or whether each boundary endpoint is attained on the same support face.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed asks for an iff support catalogue and endpoint witnesses, not a boundary plug-in heuristic.

seed_details.title: A critical dependence budget for escape from independent-source bounds
seed_details.anchor_location: Sections 3--4 explicitly polynomialize products of independent disturbance probabilities; this is the first algebraic step altered by a dependence budget.
seed_details.opportunity: Index compatibility and the risk interval by a total-variation or information budget on the joint latent law, and derive the smallest budget at which the independent interval is breached.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace latent-cell factorization by a constrained coupling problem and derive its critical budget.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches found inflation and generic constrained polynomial programs, but no budget-indexed formula for this experimental menu.
seed_details.red_team: This is merely a standard sensitivity analysis over a copula class.
seed_details.rebuttal: The proposed critical budget must jointly characterize data compatibility and endpoint escape while preserving both experimental tables, which is not supplied by a generic copula envelope.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed includes a named critical budget and exact endpoint path, avoiding sufficient-only sensitivity.

seed_details.title: Uniform inference at compatibility boundaries and endpoint ties
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 6 and Appendix C construct confidence regions for empirical probabilities and project them through the program; the paper reports conservative regions rather than tie-specific exact asymptotics.
seed_details.opportunity: Derive a local asymptotic law and uniformly valid confidence set for the entire interval when active max/min branches change.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace projection of a generic multinomial region by a directional derivative of the explicit max/min map and a contact-set calibration.
seed_details.destination_search: The target--method search found directional-bootstrap and moment-inequality tools, but no tie-inclusive result for this collider compatibility cone.
seed_details.red_team: Fang and Santos already give the bootstrap for maxima and minima.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their generic derivative theory does not by itself handle a possibly empty estimated fiber, simultaneous lower-and-upper coverage, and local approach to this feasibility boundary.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a limit-law kernel attached to a graphical bound, not a bare inference rung.

seed_details.title: The exact private-noise support complexity of collider certificates
seed_details.anchor_location: Theorem 1 and Appendix A give a general finite cardinality bound through canonical partitions; they do not minimize private support for a fixed observed menu.
seed_details.opportunity: Characterize the smallest support of private outcome noise needed to certify each rational endpoint and identify inputs attaining the worst case.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace generic canonical cardinality with a minimum common randomization of the finitely many required response probabilities.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found canonical upper bounds and Carathéodory reductions, but no menu-specific minimum-support theorem for this graph.
seed_details.red_team: Sorting the response probabilities immediately gives the minimum number of threshold atoms.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sorting supplies an upper bound; minimality permits non-threshold deterministic response patterns and requires a matching lower bound over a nondegenerate set of inputs.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed asks for an iff minimum and a worst-case region, not a single small witness.

seed_details.title: Sharp collider fusion under bounded cross-study population drift
seed_details.anchor_location: Section 5 merges observational and interventional datasets with an index variable, explicitly discussing study-specific exogenous chances; Section 7 states that EMCC returns approximate inner ranges.
seed_details.opportunity: Bound the target when the two experiments need not share one latent law but their source distributions differ by a quantified budget.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace exact equality of the two regime-specific root laws by an extremal transport coupling across study populations.
seed_details.destination_search: The search found approximate indexed-study fusion and general transport sensitivity, but no closed-form sharp interval for this collider menu.
seed_details.red_team: Allowing population drift destroys the meaning of the shared joint-intervention target.
seed_details.rebuttal: A target-population law and explicit transport budget restore a well-defined target, but specifying that law adds substantial primitives absent from the present brief.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is mathematically distinct but was dropped because the additional target-population primitives would change the posed object.

literature_map.settled: Generic finite response-function reduction, sharp polynomial optimization, linear symbolic bounds in suitable response models, and approximate multi-study fusion are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No checked source gives the exact two-table compatibility inequality, the three-branch sharp endpoints, or the universal source-preserving threshold extension for this independent-root collider.
literature_map.method_adapted: Adapt Duarte et al.'s product-disturbance polynomialization by aggregating response types into four natural-treatment strata, then adapt Sachs et al.'s symbolic primal analysis to eliminate the two remaining masses.
literature_map.writing_exemplar_used: Gresele et al.'s compatibility--ambiguity--falsifiability arc is used to motivate why separately credible causal reports must admit one joint SCM.

literature_map.settled: Projection from a shared response-function law and scalar sharp optimization are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: The checked papers do not characterize the simultaneous four-risk image under two independent shared roots.
literature_map.method_adapted: Use Gresele et al.'s shared-response projection matrices together with symbolic redundancy removal from Sachs et al.; the first unresolved move is a complete multivariate elimination.
literature_map.writing_exemplar_used: Gresele et al.'s overlapping-study setup remains the closest exposition template.

literature_map.settled: Finite canonicalization and lower-degree multilinear formulations for quasi-Markovian bounds are settled.
literature_map.unoccupied_pair: No checked source gives a finite compatibility characterization or attained all-zero interval for three source-specific collider experiments.
literature_map.method_adapted: Combine query-relevant response aggregation from Shridharan and Iyengar with product-source canonicalization from Duarte et al.; higher-order elimination remains open.
literature_map.writing_exemplar_used: Gresele et al.'s extension from two to more causal margins supplies the motivation arc.
